title: Paired-control validation and automated rollback thresholds for pinned model upgrades
creator: Asha Menon
description: Build a paired A/B validation flow for pinned model upgrades that runs the candidate variant alongside the control at a deterministic per-pin split, applies automated rollback thresholds for latency/cost/quality regressions, and surfaces an action center for operators. This ticket scopes the product requirements, success metrics, API surface, and console UX for operators to create paired experiments that: 1) deterministically map a subset of pinned requests to a candidate model while keeping the rest on the pinned control, 2) collect end-to-end telemetry (latency, token cost, sampling-based quality signal, safety hits), 3) compute real-time deltas and risk scores, and 4) execute automated rollback or tiered throttling when thresholds are breached. Applies to hosted + dedicated capacity patterns; private deployment will be delivered as a config bundle, not enforced automation. Goal: reduce human-verification time for model pins and cut rollback MTTR by 60% for routine regressions.
comments: 2026-02-20 — Asha Menon: Initial draft of goals and high-level flow. Framing as a paired-control validation to emphasize deterministic mapping for pins (vs random sampling across all traffic).

2026-02-24 — Diego Rivera: Engineering feasibility review requested. Major open questions: cost of dual-execution when KV/seq cache differs, how to route identical user sessions deterministically, and whether auto-rollback should be opt-in per-customer for Dedicated. Assigned ENG-4120 for runtime implications and ENG-4218 for routing layer work.

2026-03-02 — ML Eval (Sophie L.): Proposed quality signals: prompt-level BLEU-like scores are noisy; we'll instrument evaluation prompts set (10k synthetic + 500 customer-provided) and use embedding-based similarity and n-gram QA checks. Privacy note: customer-provided prompts must be opt-in and redacted. Added as dependency to eval-runbook.

2026-03-05 — UX (Liam C.): Draft console flows uploaded (Drive link). Key UX concepts: 1) create Paired Experiment from Pin page, 2) preview deterministic mapping table, 3) live risk dashboard with three-level alerts (info/warning/critical), 4) manual override and immediate rollback button. Need design review in Cycle 11.

2026-03-09 — Diego Rivera: Engineering spike completed. Findings: dual-execution overhead varies by model size; we can support two modes — shadow-copy (no token double-charge, uses cached KV for candidate when possible) and full-dual (exact dual inference for end-to-end parity). Recommend starting with shadow-copy for Hosted to limit cost and opt-in full-dual for Dedicated. PR: github.com/redwood/serve/pulls/6872

2026-03-12 — Security (Priya K.): Confirmed KMS policy must be extended for candidate variant logs; telemetry sampling must be encrypted at rest and PII redaction enforced. Security review required before enabling auto-rollback for Private deployments.

2026-03-14 — Asha Menon: Product decision: scope MVP to Hosted + Dedicated; Private will get the same APIs but operators must deploy the rollback agent themselves. Auto-rollback will be opt-in globally and opt-out on per-pin basis. Next: finalize API proto and console mock sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Product: Operator can create a Paired Experiment from any existing Pin and specify candidate fraction and metric thresholds (latency/cost/quality/safety).
Telemetry: System computes delta metrics (candidate vs control) with per-minute resolution and displays a rolling 30m risk score.

Automation: When thresholds breach for 3 consecutive windows, auto-rollback is triggered and an audit event is recorded. Auto-rollback must be reversible and require an explicit operator acknowledge for permanent rollbacks.
Cost: MVP dual-execution mode (shadow-copy) does not increase billed token costs for Hosted customers by default. Full-dual mode must present projected cost estimate before enabling.
Security: Telemetry sampling respects PII redaction and KMS encryption; security review completed and signed off.
Docs: PRD, runbook, and Console help pages published; SDKs updated with pairedExperimentCreate API.
